## Covered behavior

- Pure deterministic clock tests: before opening, opening instant, just before/exact closing, from-time until midnight, overnight `22:00–02:00`, grant/budget priority, window close with available base or active exception, saved usage/grant preservation, changing timezone and time, Europe/Berlin DST gap and overlap, and identical endpoints rejected.
- Repository tests: actual old schema-v1 JSON **without** an hours field, remaining allowance/credit/grant persistence and repository recreation. Existing accounting tests remain in the Gradle suite.
- Compose instrumentation: editor mode selection, invalid identical endpoints refusing Save, rule persistence across activity recreation, plus existing blocking and task-removal tests.
- Service source: receives screen wake/unlock, manual time, date and timezone events; schedules a one-shot earliest wall-clock boundary and preserves the existing bounded foreground reconciliation.

**Important distinction:** Clock-dependent acceptance is tested deterministically in the pure policy, not by setting a physical device's clock. Source-level service wiring and ordinary emulator instrumentation do not prove that a Redmi will enforce every transition while its Accessibility service is disconnected or killed. No user/device clock or personal app data was changed.

## Still unverified

Physical Redmi/HyperOS accessibility process reliability; continuous monitoring after OEM process termination; precise transition enforcement under real-device scheduling delays; API 34+ runtime behavior; overnight battery/doze behavior; in-place updates to any personally installed earlier APK. An initial emulator startup ADB attempt returned exit code 1, but the runner subsequently recovered and the Gradle instrumentation phase and entire workflow succeeded. No claim of fixing the known Redmi Accessibility disconnection is made.

The reviewed feature is in PR #3 against the current 1.0.7 development branch; no merge.
